target: fatal accidents involving Boeing commercial jets

evidence.scope: global commercial-aviation accident census under IATA methodology
evidence.observation: IATA reports six fatal accidents worldwide in 2017. Five were turboprop accidents and the remaining fatal jet accident was a cargo operation; there were no passenger fatalities on jet transport aircraft. Its annual accident table identifies Boeing 747-400 TC-MCL at Bishkek as a cargo jet hull loss.
evidence.use: annual universe and fatal-jet exhaustion evidence

evidence.publisher: Interstate Aviation Committee (IAC/MAK), Air Accident Investigation Commission
evidence.source_title: Boeing 747-412F TC-MCL 16.01.2017 investigation page and final report
evidence.observation: IAC identifies Boeing 747-412F TC-MCL, serial 32897, ACT Airlines, investigation complete, aircraft destroyed and 39 fatalities; its investigation notes crew and ground fatalities.

evidence.publisher: Boeing Commercial Airplanes, summarized by Flight Safety Foundation
evidence.source_title: 2017 worldwide commercial-jet accident statistics / ACT Airlines 747-400
evidence.observation: Boeing data report 40 commercial-jet accidents in 2017 and identify ACT Airlines 747-400 as the accident with onboard fatalities: four onboard and 35 external fatalities.
evidence.use: independent target reconciliation and external-fatality check

completeness_assessment.reason: IATA's global commercial-aviation census explicitly exhausts the 2017 fatal-jet universe to one cargo-jet accident; that accident is Boeing 747-412F TC-MCL, is confirmed by the investigating authority, and is independently reconciled against Boeing worldwide commercial-jet statistics. No unresolved target-taxonomy boundary remains for this event.

gate_effect: 2017 annual G1 cell PASS only; overall G1 remains BLOCKED until every required year passes
